summary.one_liner: A Docker image that runs an OpenVPN server with a built-in EasyRSA certificate authority, configured through a persistent data volume.
summary.what_it_does: It runs an OpenVPN server inside a Docker container and sets up an EasyRSA PKI certificate authority in a data volume. The ovpn_genconfig and ovpn_initpki scripts generate the server config, Diffie-Hellman parameters, server keys and certificates, and a TLS auth key. Client certificates are created with easyrsa build-client-full, and ovpn_getclient prints a single inline .ovpn client profile. The configuration and PKI files live in /etc/openvpn, which is declared as a volume so it can be reused or backed up. The README also describes an optional systemd service for start-on-boot and auto-restart, plus Docker Compose usage, and a DEBUG environment variable for verbose output.
use_cases: Run a self-hosted OpenVPN server in Docker
Create OpenVPN client certificates and profiles
Route client traffic through a home or cloud VPN
Keep OpenVPN and its dependencies out of the host system
Back up and reuse OpenVPN configuration and certificates
how_to_run: docker run -v $OVPN_DATA:/etc/openvpn --rm kylemanna/openvpn ovpn_getclient CLIENTNAME > CLIENTNAME.ovpn
notable: Self-contained PKI: the container creates its own EasyRSA certificate authority, Diffie-Hellman parameters and TLS auth key
Configuration and keys stored in a Docker volume, so the host filesystem is left mostly untouched and removal is a few docker commands
Client profiles are exported as a single inline .ovpn file via ovpn_getclient
Uses tun mode and net30 topology for broad client compatibility, per the README
Reference systemd service and Docker Compose setup are described in the docs
caveats: The README states the CA key is kept in the container by default; a passphrase or offline CA is recommended for stronger security
build-client-full with nopass leaves generated client keys on the server
Requires the container to run with NET_ADMIN capability and a UDP port (1194) reachable from clients
Tested mainly on older Ubuntu and Digital Ocean hosts, per the README
keywords: vpn without installing packages on host
